title: A threshold for maximal Schmidt number from spectrum
abstract: The Schmidt number quantifies the dimensionality of entanglement in bipartite quantum states. We investigate when the spectrum of a state on $\mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$ alone guarantees that its Schmidt number is not maximal. By deriving spectral bounds for $(d-1)$-block positive operators, we prove that $\mathrm{LS}_p\subseteq \mathrm{ASN}_{d-1}$ for $p\leq \lfloor d^2/2\rfloor$, where $\mathrm{LS}_p$ denotes the set of states whose largest eigenvalue does not exceed the sum of their $p$ smallest eigenvalues, and $\mathrm{ASN}_{d-1}$ denotes the set of states whose Schmidt number remains at most $d-1$ under all global unitaries. This also yields a simple sufficient condition involving only the largest eigenvalue. As an application, we show that states satisfying the reduction criterion under arbitrary global unitaries belong to $\mathrm{ASN}_{d-1}$ in every dimension. This subsumes the earlier result that absolutely positive partial transpose states belong to $\mathrm{ASN}_{d-1}$. The global unitary requirement is nevertheless essential: for every $d\geq3$, we construct states of maximal Schmidt number satisfying the reduction criterion on both subsystems.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes deep connections between the spectral properties of a bipartite quantum state and its entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number. It proves that certain spectral conditions are sufficient to bound entanglement, while also showing that the global unitary requirement is essential for these bounds to hold. The results refine our understanding of spectral obstructions to entanglement.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spectral conditions on a bipartite quantum state that guarantee its Schmidt number is not maximal, particularly comparing spectral bounds ($	ext{LS}_p$) to entanglement measures ($	ext{ASN}_{d-1}$).
main_result: It proves that certain spectral conditions, such as $	ext{LS}_p \subseteq 	ext{ASN}_{d-1}$ for $p \le \lfloor d^2/2 floor$, and establishes that states satisfying the absolute reduction criterion ($	ext{ARED}$) belong to $	ext{ASN}_{d-1}$.
method: The analysis heavily relies on spectral theory, deriving bounds for block positive operators, and using techniques related to the Hahn–Banach separation theorem to establish inclusions between different classes of quantum states.
model_or_system: The study focuses on bipartite quantum states $ho$ acting on $\mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$, analyzing entanglement quantified by the Schmidt number ($	ext{SN}(ho)$).
key_observables: Schmidt number ($	ext{SN}(ho)$), eigenvalues of the state ($\lambda_i$), and spectral quantities derived from block positivity.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the subsystems, and the index $p$ used in the spectral condition $	ext{LS}_p$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares spectral conditions to entanglement witnesses, and the necessity of the global unitary requirement is highlighted by constructing counterexamples.
